title: Symmetric pair contraction
statement: Let $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous on $[0,1]$ and nonnegative there, and suppose that whenever $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$, $P(a)\le\frac12\bigl(\sqrt{P(a+b)^2+b^2}+\sqrt{P(a-b)^2+b^2}\bigr)$. For real $a,b,t$ with $a+b,a-b,t\in[0,1]$ and vectors $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, the symmetric average lengths satisfy $L(t,(tb)^2)\le L(1,b^2)$.
hypotheses_covered: For all real $a,b$ with $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$, the stated inequality for $P(a)$ holds
replaced: For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $a,b,t,c\in\mathbb R$, and $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, define $L(t,c)=\frac12\bigl(\sqrt{P(a+tb)^2+c+\|u+tv\|_2^2}+\sqrt{P(a-tb)^2+c+\|u-tv\|_2^2}\bigr)$. Assume $P\ge0$ on $[0,1]$ and, whenever $z\pm d\in[0,1]$, $P(z)\le\bigl(\sqrt{P(z+d)^2+d^2}+\sqrt{P(z-d)^2+d^2}\bigr)/2$. If $P$ is also continuous on $[0,1]$, $a\pm b\in[0,1]$, and $0\le t\le1$, then $L(t,(tb)^2)\le L(1,b^2)$.
